messages:
matt: Heads-up — ran a quick INT6 bring-up for `switchback-11b` on the high-throughput fleet. Big cost delta (≈2.6x token $ reduction vs fp16) but a few worrying quality signals on longform summarization slices. Trying to decide whether to proceed to a staged canary or pause and triage. thoughts?

jia: can you paste the slice metrics? curious which slices regressed the most. :eyes:

matt: sure, quick paste from smoke run: `summary_long` +6.4% ROUGE-L drop, hallucination rate +3.2pp on entity recall, latency median -28%, cost per 1k tokens ~-62%. Overall pass on short-turn chat slices.

sam: ok that's significant for product. do we have a priming/temperature mismatch? sometimes quantized models get sticky completions on long context.

claire: if product sees +6% rouge drop on long summaries that's user-visible. recommend a hybrid routing: keep INT6 for <512 tokens, route >512 to fp16 or 13b variant. can we shadow route first?

ben: routing ok but also check KVCACHE perf. INT6 kernel changes could be evicting kv pages under long sequences. matt — did you capture tracer logs?

matt: pasted a short log snippet below:

```
[2026-03-21 14:02:13] request_id=abc123 seq_len=1024 model=switchback-11b-int6 step=gen token=... latency_kv_miss=12.4ms
[2026-03-21 14:02:13] request_id=abc123 step=gen kv_cache_evictions=3
```

matt: kv evictions were non-zero on the failing slices.

eval-bot: quick-eval finished: baseline=fp16-switchback-11b, compare=int6-switchback-11b. sample=5k long-summary slices. metrics: ROUGE-L -6.2%, HallRate +3.1pp, BLEU -1.9%, P95 latency -30%. full report: https://internal/reports/3332109876 (flags: kvcache_eviction_high)

sam: thanks. two parallel paths: 1) engineer-level fix — look at kvcache allocation and kernel scheduling to avoid evictions; 2) product-level mitigate — hybrid routing + canary. both are doable but infra fix may take a few days.

jia: for GTN (growth/product) guidance: recommend we present unit-econ tradeoff with a concrete holdback plan. e.g., show 2.6x cost savings vs expected user impact (estimated 2–6% quality drop on long summaries). propose a 10% canary on low-risk customers and 0% exposed for long-summary heavy customers until we have mitigations.

claire: agreed. also add a short-term rollback flag: `model: switchback-11b-int6; override: route_long_to=fp16-switchback-11b`. product can toggle via console.

ben: ops note — warmstart nodes for INT6 to avoid first-request jitter. I'll trigger a warmpool of 10 GPUs for the canary window. deploy-bot, please schedule a canary in us-west2 at 9am PST tomorrow.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary: switchback-11b-int6 -> 10% traffic, warmpool=10, region=us-west2, start=2026-03-22T09:00:00-08:00. Canary window=48h.

matt: action items I captured: 1) eng (ben/sam) investigate kvcache kernel scheduling + test patch (48h). 2) infra (ben) warmpool + deploy canary (done). 3) eval (jia) run targeted synthetic long-summary set + user-sim for 48h. 4) product (claire) prepare GTN messaging + holdback list. 5) rollback route flag ready.

jia: I'll run the targeted eval now; will post a short signal dashboard (slice breakdown + expected impact) before canary start.

sam: if eng patch looks small we can attempt an in-canary hotfix — but prefer triage first.

matt: thanks team. let's reconvene after the first 12h of canary or earlier if eval flags exceed thresholds: ROUGE-L drop >4% on any critical slice or HallRate +2pp.

claire: noted. product will label customers in GTN as `long-summary-sensitive` so we can exclude them from canary.

ben: will post kvcache traces and a patch PR if we find scheduling bug. tagging @sam for review. :thumbsup:

matt: perfect. thanks all — feel better about a measured canary than wholesale rollout.
